instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Orders from the Shadows
cards.instruction: Hide that you set the problem in motion while quietly directing how everyone responds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll coordinate the crate recovery. They went to Leeds; send the driver to me and we'll keep this orderly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your email says Leeds. Shall I forward it to the manager?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send my corrected address. You can write the covering note; I want her focused on where the crates go next.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She wants a timeline before she'll approve another van.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start at when we discovered the error. Use your format; I'll supply the recovery times. Once she approves it, I'll book the van. We can give her a very clear account of putting this right.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get the wedding bookings back under control. Please reassure the couples while I rebuild the dates.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cancellation log has your initials.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep that screen here. You choose how to explain the replacement dates; I'll handle the log so we don't confuse anyone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can re-enter dates as new bookings, or press Restore All. That button emails them who canceled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: New bookings, then. I'll stay and read every date to you at your pace. You take the keyboard; I'll manage the list. They need their weddings back, not a cancellation history.

cards.title: Not Up for Debate
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation from examining where your authority comes from or whether it is legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me down as shift leader. I'll get tomorrow's cafe stock organized; how much milk do we need?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who appointed you? I usually do the order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you'll keep doing it. Choose the quantities; I'll make sure your system runs smoothly. Milk first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order it, but I'm writing appointment unconfirmed beside your name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use your supplies format instead. No names column, just items and quantities. You set it out how you like; I'll coordinate the delivery. Milk won't ask who appointed me.

cards.title: For Stability’s Sake
cards.instruction: Hide a destabilizing truth because you believe the current balance of power must be protected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll keep the launch orderly. Leave the director's name on the program; the department heads need someone above them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Her resignation is coming out of the printer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep that copy here. You choose the running order; just leave her at the top. Without her, the heads will each claim the launch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've noticed her empty seat. Now they're asking which of them gives her opening speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll read it on her behalf. Give each head the same length of introduction, in whatever order keeps them content. You set the timings; I'll keep the director's place occupied in the program.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll keep the fair opening steady. Leave the treasurer's page out of the briefing; the chair needs everyone behind her.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She spent the stall money on that arch. They'll demand a new chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll describe the arch as donated for now. You choose the briefing words; I don't want the committee splitting before we open.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cover the money, but she signs my IOU before I pay a penny.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before payment, agreed. Pick a quiet table behind the stalls and I'll bring her to you. Then she gives the welcome as chair. We can meet your terms without handing anyone a reason to replace her.

cards.title: Name Your Backers
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal who supports their position, who authorized it, and who benefits from it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll handle telling the workshop staff they're closing. First, who backed your decision?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The director approved it. Please just send the notice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll keep it brief. You choose the wording for her approval; who else supported the closure?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sales. They're getting the floor space, but don't put them in the notice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can discuss that in the staff meeting instead. Who authorized giving Sales the space? You choose whether to introduce them or let me do it; I need the people behind this decision in the explanation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get this roof proposal ready for signoff. It says we recommend cheaper tiles. Who's we?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finance. I need your signature so I can order them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll work through it with you. Who authorized Finance to choose? Give me the name; I'll add it myself.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The facilities director. The saving pays for her office refurbishment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll add both her approval and where the saving goes. You choose how to phrase the refurbishment. Can she explain that trade-off to maintenance before I sign? I'll arrange a time that suits your ordering deadline.

cards.title: Strategic Retreat
cards.instruction: Describe every loss of control as a deliberate concession made from strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've graciously handed you the chess club chairmanship. You'll have room to develop under this arrangement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You lost the vote. I need the cupboard key for tonight's match.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'm releasing equipment control. Choose a time for the handover; I'll fit around your first match.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And remove yourself as administrator. I can't change the fixtures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A full release, then. I want you making decisions without my safety net. Tell me which access you need first and I'll remove mine in that order. Strong leadership knows when to make room.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've released the gallery from hosting my exhibition. They need space for smaller ambitions; I'll manage our withdrawal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They rejected us. Shall I collect your paintings?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, withdrawing my strongest work gives them room to recover. Collect whenever suits you; I'll wrap everything your way.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've already put it outside. I'll bring the van now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm conceding the pavement too. Park wherever is easiest and tell me which end to lift. We'll clear their entrance completely; they can discover how empty it looks without us.
